scientific_question: Can the dense ambient Muon momentum and compression-error state that causally closes the full-MLP loss gap be stored blockwise at low precision without changing its useful directions?

interpretation_contract.mechanism: Blockwise scalar quantization retains every ambient coordinate and therefore does not impose the low-rank, sparse, shared-orbit, or procedural-chart direction restrictions already falsified. It changes precision only.
interpretation_contract.pass: At least one arm meets every raw-state, state-only Muon-polar, and storage threshold. Select the smallest passing persistent representation, then authorize only exact-resume codec implementation, focused tests, and an exact-config MFU/peak-VRAM gate.
interpretation_contract.fail: No arm preserves both temporal-state families and the induced Muon polar direction. Close direct blockwise low-precision state and do not launch a training run.
interpretation_contract.boundary: The terminal checkpoint contains no next-step gradient, so the polar metric is a state-only proxy. A pass is necessary but not sufficient for loss preservation; one 124M LM run remains mandatory after implementation and systems gates.
interpretation_contract.storage: Eight-bit values use an actual signed-int8 container. Six- and four-bit byte counts assume packed storage and cannot be promoted without a packed codec. All arms store one FP16 max-absolute scale per contiguous block.
